claim:
Let \(0<\omega<1\), and let \(L_\omega=(\mathbb R^2,N_\omega)\) be the two-dimensional Lorentz endpoint plane
\[
N_\omega(s,t)=\max\{|s|,|t|\}+\omega\min\{|s|,|t|\}.
\]
For \(1\le p<\infty\), define the Gao-type constant
\[
c_{\mathrm{NJ}}^{(p)}(L_\omega)
=
\inf_{x,y\in S_{L_\omega}}
\frac{N_\omega(x+y)^p+N_\omega(x-y)^p}{2^p}.
\]
Then \(c_{\mathrm{NJ}}^{(1)}(L_\omega)=1\). For \(p>1\), writing \(p'=p/(p-1)\),
\[
c_{\mathrm{NJ}}^{(p)}(L_\omega)
=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{(1+\omega)^p}
{\bigl((1+\omega)^{p'}+(1-\omega)^{p'}\bigr)^{p-1}},
&0<\omega\le\sqrt2-1,\\[3mm]
\bigl(1+\omega^{p'}\bigr)^{1-p},
&\sqrt2-1\le\omega<1.
\end{cases}
\]
The phase transition \(\omega=\sqrt2-1\) is independent of \(p\).
integrity: The proof is self-contained. An exhaustive eight-facet dual-norm argument gives the global lower bound, Hölder optimization gives the sharp branch values, and explicit unit pairs attain them. No finite sampling or numerical optimization is used for correctness.
scientific_limitations: The theorem covers only the real two-dimensional Lorentz endpoint r=1, with 0<omega<1 and finite Gao exponent p>=1. It does not settle the remaining interior Lorentz range 1<r<2. A later equivalent computation under different terminology remains a residual bibliographic risk.
title: All Gao-type constants at the polyhedral two-dimensional Lorentz endpoint
